newsitem.title: CANADA: FOCUS-CanWest eyes U.S., Alberta market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-CanWest eyes U.S., Alberta market.

text.p: On the heels of expansion into Australia and New Zealand, CanWest Global Communications Corp chairman Israel Asper said on Thursday he was determined to gain a U.S. foothold and a larger slice of the Canadian broadcasting pie.
Asper said it was no secret the company was working hard on an entry vehicle into the huge U.S. market.
"Nothing is too outrageous for us to consider," Asper told reporters following the annual meeting of the Winnipeg, Manitoba -based broadcaster.
Asper said CanWest was not beating the bushes for acquisitions in the United States but was considering every option, from broadcasting, to programming, to sales.
"We're making progress, but I'd like to advance that, escalate it, and the only way we're going to do it is to be able to get American stations," Asper said.
He declined to say whether CanWest was working on a deal with Rupert Murdoch's Fox network, a unit of News Corp.
"Not specifically," said Asper. "We talk to Fox everyday."

CanWest last week raised its economic interest in Australia's Network Ten to 76 percent from 66 percent. In New Zealand, CanWest recently acquired total ownership of TV3 and won the right to launch another network in that country.

But expansion have gone less smoothly on the homefront. On Tuesday the Canadian government denied a CanWest appeal to overturn an earlier decision by Canadian regulators which denied CanWest a television broadcasting license in Alberta. The license was won by Brandon, Manitoba's family-owned Craig Broadcast Systems Inc.

Asper said CanWest would get its product into Alberta despite the failed licence application, pointing to promising comments made by Canadian Heritage Minister Sheila Copps directing the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission to consider the need for a third national TV system, which CanWest has been seeking.

"We're obviously going to be in Alberta, there are other options," said Asper. "Obviously if we applied for and became a national system, we would be able to pipe our programming into Alberta by virtue of own underground affiliates."
Asper said another takeover bid for CanWest's arch-rival WIC Western International Communications Ltd, which has TV stations in the same Alberta market, was not on CanWest's immediate agenda.

"We were expecting to have our own licenses in Alberta... but we've retained our shares in WIC, and we're obviously monitoring that one fairly closely, because WIC is an important customer of ours, as well as somebody that we wanted to own."

A bid by CanWest for the family-controlled WIC was blocked last year by a court ruling against CanWest's attempt to have voting rights awarded to WIC's non-voting shareholders. An appeal will be heard in February.
Asper said CanWest was in the nice position of having a lot of options to get its product into Alberta.
"We think that decision (on the court appeal) is many months away, and in the meantime we may enter into other arrangements with WIC, or we may enter into other arrangements with Craig Broadcasting."
